column2: Mixed with paste, a decoction of neem is for vomiting; water of oily, sweated barley should be given as a purgative.
If applied otherwise it causes weak digestion, heaviness and distaste. One should drink with warm water powder of pathya, rock salt and krishna.
The purge called Narachaka is the best, destroying all diseases. The proven combinations shown by Atreya to the sages — destroyers of all diseases, chief of all combinations — are indeed by Sushruta.
A man who drinks uchchata with honey, a karsha, living on milk, conquers death; or nirgundi with honey, ghee or milk conquers disease and death.
One should drink a karsha of palasha oil with honey for six months; living on milk the man would live five hundred (years), a thousand-year life.
One should drink juice of jyotishmati leaf with milk, triphala with honey and ghee likewise, a pala of shatavari powder;
or with honey, ghee and milk, nirgundi conquers disease and death. The five parts of neem powder steeped in khadira decoction,
a karsha with bhringaraja juice conquers disease and one becomes undying. Rudantika with ghee and honey, living on milk, conquers death.
A karsha of haritaki powder steeped in bhringaraja juices, taken with ghee and honey, gives three hundred years and conquers disease.
Varahika, bhringaraja juice, iron powder, shatavari with ghee — a karsha gives five hundred years; shatavari powder as made;
steeped in bhringaraja with honey and ghee, it gives three hundred. Calcined copper equal to mercury, sulphur and kumari,
rubbed with juices, two gunjas with ghee, one has five hundred years. Ashvagandha a pala, oil with ghee and sugar, gives a hundred years;
a pala of punarnava powder with honey, ghee and milk — drink; a pala of ashoka powder with honey, ghee and milk removes affliction.
Sesame oil with honey as nasal medicine gives black hair for a hundred; a karsha of akshaka with honey and ghee; drinking milk, one lives a hundred years.
Having eaten abhaya with jaggery, with ghee, honey and sweet things, living on milk-food, with black hair, free of disease, he has five hundred years.
Drinking a pala of kushmandika powder with honey, ghee and milk for a month, living on milk food, one has a thousand years free of disease.
Shaluka powder with bhringa, ghee and honey gives a hundred years; nasal oil of pungent tumbi, a karsha, gives two hundred years.
Triphala, pippali and ginger taken give three hundred years; the earlier combination of shatavari gives a thousand years and great strength.
With chitraka likewise the earlier; so too from ginger and vidanga; with iron, bhringaraja, bala, the five of neem;
with khadira, nirgundi, kantakari and vasaka, with punarnava or its juices, made as a pill,
powder with ghee or honey, jaggery and the like, or with water; with the mantra "Om hrum sah," by mantra, the king of combinations;
the Mritasanjivani regimen would be the conqueror of disease and death. Oceans of regimens attended by gods, demons and sages; he taught the Gaja-ayurveda (elephant medicine) to Palakapya, Angaraja.
Planets are in neighing and likewise Vasuki is in the chest. Fasting, the rider should worship the horse and recite in the right ear:

Horse, you are king of the Gandharvas; hear my word, go. You are born of a Gandharva family; do not be a defiler of the family.
agnipuran:286:14	By the true word of Brahmins, and by Soma, Garuda, Rudra, Varuna, and the strength of the wind,
agnipuran:286:15	and the radiance of fire, remember your birth, horse. Remember you are a king's son; remember the true word;
agnipuran:286:16	remember the Varuni maiden; remember the Kaustubha jewel when the milk ocean was churned by gods and demons;
agnipuran:286:17	there you were born in the divine family; keep your own word. Born in the horse family, be my eternal friend.
agnipuran:286:18	Hear this, friend; be accomplished for me, steed; guard victory and me; bring success in battle.
agnipuran:286:19	Mounting your back the demons were slain by the gods of old; now mounting you I shall conquer the enemy's army.
Having whispered in the ear and having bewildered the enemies too, the rider should lead the horse around; he should ride it; victory is from battle.
The faults arising from their own bodies in horses mostly are removed with great effort, and virtues again by the best riders;
virtues arisen from the best riders appear as if innate; other riders destroy even innate virtues.
One knows the virtues, another knows the faults; the fortunate wise one knows the horse; the dull-minded —
one who does not know the work, does not know the means, is attached to speed, over-angry, delights in heavy beating in an opening, is not praised even by me.
One who knows the means, knows the mind, pure, destroying faults, devoted to gaining virtues, always skilled in all works,
having taken it by the rein, entering the riding ground, should be ridden by his own rider by left and right distinctions.
Having mounted, the best horse should not be beaten suddenly; from beating it gets both, and from fear bewilderment arises.
In the morning the rider should lift the rein with a leap and move it, slowly, slowly, not without need, holding the rein day by day.
Reassurance is told; the conciliatory approach is applied to the horse; beating with the whip and the like is the stick; giving and endurance of time.
When the joints are purified one after the other, one should do the next. One should apply, on the tongue, in riding the horse, without engaging;
the rein of a hundred other virtues should be made to enter along with the corners of the mouth. One should ride, making it forget, the relaxed ones slowly, slowly.
When the horse lacks the tongue-part one should release the tongue-knot; one should release the tightness until it does not release the bit.
One should make a hundred chest-protections and the one who releases the saliva; whose face is up, his chest-protection is not loose;
having made it, the best rider should ride with sportive look; for him with the left front joined with left rein,
whoever makes the rear foot, the right is taken by it. By this order one who serves with the left rein,
by that too the foot is the left taken. If the front foot is released, a very firm seat arises.
Those taken in difficult ways — mota, natakayana; without the left, khalikara, by hana and guna.
The horse's own nature is turning the face forward; thus there are no reasons for foot-taking of horses.
Seeing a horse trusting, pressing the seat firmly, stopping the foot at the mouth, looking is beneficial in taking.
Pressing firmly with the two reins and pulling the rein it is taken; by binding it the pair of feet, thus it is called vakvana.
Having joined the feet with the rein, having released the rein, as wished; where there is application of the outer heel, that is held beating.
Knowing the rout in the disorder, the wise one by this order, with the fourth mota, this rule is ordained.
A horse that does not put down the foot in a light circle should be made to take the desired foot with mota and udvakkana.
One who, having made the firm seat, goes slowly taking — where it is taken by gathering, that is called sangrahana.
Having struck at the side by a blow, standing in place, with a distracted mind, pulling the rein with the foot — the taking of the thorn-drink.
The horse that rises with this foot from the heel-foot, taken by bridling, that is desired as khalikara.
In the three gaits it takes the foot, not as wished; striking with a staff, where it is taken, that is dense.
Having bridled with the four, the horse by another rein, being made to breathe out is taken elsewhere — that would be again called ucchasana.
The outer nature thrown out, walking in that direction, having engaged it, one should make it take: that is held mukhavyavartana.
Having then made it take the foot in the three, in order, one should accomplish in the five paths, in circles and the rest, in order.
Having made the knee-high face-up ride, the wise should ride it loose; as long as lightness is in the limbs, so long he should ride that horse.
Soft at the shoulder, light at the mouth, loose in all joints — when it is under control with its rider, then he should hold the horse.
It should not leave the rear foot when it is good, then; the drawing should be done here with both hands and the rein.
There, as a three-fold stands, a horse with raised neck and equal face, rear feet on the ground and standing in the air,
then one should hold it and ride firmly with the fist. A horse drawn suddenly thus that does not stand,
and throws its body about, one should discipline it by circling turns; and one that throws the shoulder in riding should be stopped by the rein.
Cow-dung, salt, urine, boiled, mixed with earth — a body-smear that destroys bites of flies and the like and fatigue.
In the middle for kinds like Bhadra, a gruel should be given by the rider. Sight of a fearful one, lack of energy, hunger of the horse;
as it is controlled, so is the training; over-ridden ones perish; ones not ridden are not trained; and one should ride tall-mouthed ones.
Having pressed the horse with both knees, with steady fist; gomutra, kutila, veni, padmamandala, malika,
panchaulukhalika should be made; they are greatly proud. Contracted and expanded, curved as fit,
valgita and avalgita, and shota are thus declared. The course is a hundred bows; eighty, ninety likewise.
The Bhadra horse is easily trained; the Manda has a single mind for the stick; the Mriga horse has deer-like shanks; the Sankirna accompanies them.
A horse that eats sugar, honey and parched rice, fragrant, pure, is a Brahmin; a spirited horse is a Kshatriya; one trained and intelligent...
